_about: How the NYC 311 sample (data/raw/nyc311_2025-03-01_to_2025-03-07.csv) is replayed into Murang'a. Implemented twice: by `manage.py replay_311` (through the real app, ward lookup and state machine) and independently by scripts/verify_analytics.py (pandas + shapely). The two must produce identical dashboard figures. Full prose in docs/replay.md.

dataset.name: NYC 311 Service Requests from 2010 to Present
dataset.query: created_date 2025-03-01T00:00 to 2025-03-08T00:00, complaint_type in the seven types below, latitude not null
dataset.licence: NYC Open Data, public, no restrictions on use

timestamps: created_date and closed_date are NYC local wall-clock times; they are read as Africa/Nairobi wall-clock times, so office-hours patterns line up with Murang'a working hours.

transform._about: Linear map of the NYC bounding box onto Murang'a's bounding box (from the GADM ward extent). Keeps the spatial clustering of real complaints. Points that land outside every ward are dropped as outside_county, the same rule the live form applies.

rules: 1. Look up (complaint_type, descriptor); an exact descriptor match wins over '*'. No match: skip as unmapped.
2. Map status with status_map. Unknown status: skip as unknown_status.
3. A closed row needs closed_date >= created_date; otherwise skip as bad_dates. closed_date on a non-closed row is ignored.
4. Transform latitude/longitude; if the point is in no ward, skip as outside_county.
5. History written: pending at created_date; in_progress at created_date if the mapped status is in_progress or closed; resolved and then closed at closed_date if closed.
6. due_at is computed by the app's own deadline rules from created_date and the category's target.
